html:
The Seven Years' War was a world war of 1756 to 1763, fought in Europe, North America, India, the Caribbean and the Philippines. On one side were Britain and Prussia; on the other France, Austria, Russia, Sweden and, from 1762, Spain. It decided that Britain, not France, would lead overseas.

It began in North America in 1754, where it is called the French and Indian War, over the Ohio valley. In 1755 the British began the expulsion of the Acadians from Nova Scotia. In Europe, Austria allied with its old enemy France to win back Silesia from Prussia, but Frederick the Great held on through years of near defeat. Britain paid him subsidies and defended the king's German homeland of Hanover.

Britain won the war overseas:

  • Quebec fell in 1759 and Montreal in 1760, ending New France.
  • In India, Robert Clive's win at Plassey in 1757 gave the East India Company Bengal, and the French were beaten in the south.
  • In 1762 British forces took Havana and Manila from Spain.

The Peace of Paris of 1763 gave Britain Canada and the land east of the Mississippi, and Spain gave up Florida to get Havana back. France handed Louisiana west of the river to Spain. Britain then taxed its American colonies to pay its war debts, which led to the American Revolution, and France's debts weighed on it until 1789.
